content_voiceover: This is the Hokusai VTE Cancer trial, comparing edoxaban to dalteparin for treatment of venous thromboembolism in cancer patients over a full year of follow up. The main graph tracks the combined endpoint of recurrent venous thromboembolism or major bleeding, and the inset zooms in on the lower end of that scale so you can see the early separation more clearly. Both curves rise together for the first month or so, then edoxaban, the solid blue line, tracks slightly below dalteparin, the dashed red line, through much of the first year, though the two curves converge again by around day two seventy before diverging once more toward the end. The number at risk table below shows steady attrition in both arms from about five hundred twenty patients down to under two hundred by day three sixty, which is typical for an oncology population given competing mortality. This trial was one of the pivotal studies establishing that a direct oral anticoagulant could be a reasonable alternative to low molecular weight heparin in cancer associated thrombosis.
keypoints: Hokusai VTE Cancer trial: edoxaban versus dalteparin, one year follow up
Composite endpoint: recurrent VTE or major bleeding
Edoxaban tracks slightly below dalteparin for most of the year
Curves converge around day 270 before diverging again
Established DOACs as an alternative to LMWH in cancer-associated thrombosis
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the Hokusai VTE Cancer trial compared edoxaban to dalteparin over one year using a composite endpoint of recurrent VTE or major bleeding, with edoxaban generally tracking slightly favorably, and it helped establish DOACs as a reasonable alternative to LMWH in cancer associated thrombosis.
